name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt near 5.22% on 11 Nov, about 22bp lower over a month; long yields still high; no weak auction found
state: The 10-year gilt yield held near 5.22% on 11 Nov as markets leaned towards another Bank of England rise in December, about 22bp lower than a month earlier and inside the Normal band for 10-year moves (Trading Economics). The 30-year yield was about 5.65% on 11 Nov, some 27bp lower over the month but still near its highest levels in decades (The Private Banker). The BoE raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov (CNBC). With no weak auction or BoE intervention found, Watch is kept for long yields near multi-decade highs.
for_you: High gilt yields tend to keep fixed mortgage rates and government borrowing costs elevated. Annuity rates and savings rates also track gilts. This describes market conditions only and is not advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: 30y gilt near multi-decade highs (~5.65% on 11 Nov); 10y moved ~22bp in a month, below the 40bp line

sources.title: The Private Banker — Gilt yields hold near 5.2% as traders lean toward a December BoE hike
CNBC — Bank of England hikes interest rate for the first time since Iran war

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
